newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Beijing must acknowledge China split - Taiwan's Lee.
newsitem.headline: Beijing must acknowledge China split - Taiwan's Lee.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui on Monday urged communist Beijing to accept that China is divided and acknowledge his island's sovereignty, saying only this would lead to better ties and the goal of national unification.

Lee, addressing the constitutional assembly, urged Taiwan's business community to put the survival of the Nationalist-ruled island's democracy ahead of profits, saying investors should "refrain from temptation" in the communist mainland.

Lee said Beijing need not worry about Taiwan declaring independence, saying the sovereignty of its exiled Republic of China has been a fact for 86 years. "There is no need nor requirement to seek independence," Lee said.
"We will never waver in our insistence on a single China that is unified as a new China through democracy, freedom and the equitable distribution of wealth," Lee said.
Lee said Beijing's People's Republic of China must accept the continued existence of the Republic of China on Taiwan despite its 1949 civil war defeat on the mainland.

"We have made a clear definition that we are two equal political entities. This concept not only meets the political reality that the two sides are under separate rule. It also accords with the goal of democratic unification specified in (Taiwan's) national unification guidelines.
"Whether relations across the Taiwan strait can have a genuine interaction depends on whether the Chinese communsist authorities can practically face the reality of one China divided," Lee said.
